review:
SUMMARY: 13 confirmed bugs found across queue implementations, scheduler utilities, backpressure helpers, and collection classes. Issues range from index corruption and NPEs to race conditions, memory leaks, and silent hangs.

POINTS:
- [src/main/java/io/reactivex/rxjava4/operators/SpscLinkedArrayQueue.java:286] offer(first, second) writes the second element to the link slot when the producer index wraps, corrupting the buffer chain [— fix: wrap pi + 1 with calcWrappedOffset/mask before soElement]
- [src/main/java/io/reactivex/rxjava4/internal/schedulers/SchedulerToExecutorService.java:31-41] Scheduler.toExecutorService() passes null for workerStore, causing immediate NPE in execute()/shutdown() [— fix: initialize workerStore with new AtomicReference<>()]
- [src/main/java/io/reactivex/rxjava4/internal/util/Pow2.java:34] roundToPowerOfTwo(Integer.MAX_VALUE) returns Integer.MIN_VALUE due to 1 << 31, causing NegativeArraySizeException [— fix: clamp/overflow-check values > 2^30 to return a valid positive power of two]
- [src/main/java/io/reactivex/rxjava4/internal/schedulers/SchedulerToExecutorService.java:44-54] shutdown() uses workerStore.get() instead of getAndSet() in the first branch, missing concurrently-set workers [— fix: use getAndSet(SHUTDOWN) atomically to dispose and update state]
- [src/main/java/io/reactivex/rxjava4/internal/schedulers/SchedulerToExecutorService.java:192] invokeAny() throws IllegalStateException due to misused CompletableFuture.exceptionNow() on normal completion [— fix: replace with proper join()/get() handling to retrieve results]
- [src/main/java/io/reactivex/rxjava4/internal/util/AppendOnlyLinkedArrayList.java:167] forEachWhile(S, BiPredicate) throws NPE on a full last chunk due to missing null check [— fix: add if (a == null) return; after advancing to the next chunk]
- [src/main/java/io/reactivex/rxjava4/internal/schedulers/CachedScheduler.java:126-141] evictExpiredWorkers breaks on first non-expired worker, skipping later expired workers in the FIFO queue and leaking memory [— fix: remove early break and iterate entire queue]
- [src/main/java/io/reactivex/rxjava4/internal/util/BackpressureHelper.java:53] multiplyCap(0, Long.MAX_VALUE) throws ArithmeticException from division by zero in overflow guard [— fix: add a != 0 && check before u / a != b]
- [src/main/java/io/reactivex/rxjava4/internal/schedulers/CachedScheduler.java:251] ThreadWorker.expirationTime lacks volatile, causing stale reads and missed evictions across threads [— fix: declare field as volatile]
- [src/main/java/io/reactivex/rxjava4/internal/subscriptions/ArrayCompositeSubscription.java:100] isDisposed() throws IndexOutOfBoundsException on capacity-0 instances [— fix: guard with if (length() == 0) return true; before accessing get(0)]
- [src/main/java/io/reactivex/rxjava4/internal/operators/flowable/FlowableSampleTimed.java:190-196] wip counter grows unbounded when timer fires faster than drain, silently hanging onComplete() [— fix: ensure wip.decrementAndGet() is called unconditionally after the increment check]
- [src/main/java/io/reactivex/rxjava4/internal/util/VolatileSizeArrayList.java:130] set() skips lazySet(list.size()), causing memory visibility failures for concurrent readers [— fix: call lazySet(list.size()) after list.set()]
- [src/main/java/io/reactivex/rxjava4/operators/SpscArrayQueue.java:87-89] offer(E, E) is non-atomic, leaving v1 in the queue if v2 fails due to capacity [— fix: check capacity for both elements upfront and add atomically or fail both]

suspicions.observation: BackpressureHelper.multiplyCap() at line 53 does `u / a != b` inside a guard `((a | b) >>> 31) != 0`. When a=0 and b > 2^31, the guard passes (since b >>> 31 != 0), then `u / a` becomes `0 / 0` which throws ArithmeticException.
suspicions.suspected_bug: multiplyCap(0, Long.MAX_VALUE) throws ArithmeticException due to division by zero instead of returning 0 (the correct capped product).

suspicions.observation: In SpscLinkedArrayQueue.offer(T first, T second), the code does `pi = calcWrappedOffset(p, m)` then `soElement(buffer, pi + 1, second)` without wrapping `pi + 1`. When producer index p wraps around (p & mask == mask, i.e., pi == p2capacity-1), `pi + 1` equals `p2capacity` which is the link slot of the buffer (buffer size is p2capacity+1, indices 0..p2capacity, with p2capacity being the link position). The same bug exists in the resize branch at line 295: `soElement(newBuffer, pi + 1, second)`.
suspicions.suspected_bug: offer(first, second) writes the second element into the buffer's link slot when the producer index wraps around, corrupting the linked buffer chain.

suspicions.observation: AppendOnlyLinkedArrayList.forEachWhile(S state, BiPredicate) uses `for (;;) { for (int i = 0; i < c; i++) { ... } a = (Object[])a[c]; }` with no null check on `a` before the inner loop. Unlike the other forEachWhile variant which uses `while (a != null)`, this one will NPE when traversing a full chunk followed by null (i.e., the last chunk is completely filled with values).
suspicions.suspected_bug: forEachWhile(S, BiPredicate) throws NullPointerException when called on a list where the last chunk is completely full, because it lacks a null check on `a` before the inner for-loop.

suspicions.observation: CachedScheduler.ThreadWorker.expirationTime is a plain long field (not volatile) accessed from multiple threads: setExpirationTime() is called from the CachedWorkerPool.release() method (scheduler worker thread) while getExpirationTime() is called from CachedWorkerPool.evictExpiredWorkers() running in the evictor thread.
suspicions.suspected_bug: Race condition on ThreadWorker.expirationTime: stale reads may cause workers to never be evicted or be evicted prematurely, because the evictor thread may not see updated expiration times due to lack of visibility (no volatile, no happens-before relationship).

suspicions.observation: Pow2.roundToPowerOfTwo(int value) does `1 << (32 - Integer.numberOfLeadingZeros(value - 1))`. For any input value > 2^30 (e.g., Integer.MAX_VALUE), `numberOfLeadingZeros(value - 1)` returns 1, so the shift is `1 << 31` which equals Integer.MIN_VALUE (negative). Using this result as array capacity causes NegativeArraySizeException.
suspicions.suspected_bug: roundToPowerOfTwo(Integer.MAX_VALUE) returns Integer.MIN_VALUE (negative) instead of 0x80000000 or a valid power-of-two, causing NegativeArraySizeException when callers like SpscArrayQueue or OpenHashSet use it to allocate arrays.

suspicions.observation: ArrayCompositeSubscription.isDisposed() only checks if get(0) == SubscriptionHelper.CANCELLED. But dispose() sets ALL slots to CANCELLED sequentially. If a concurrent thread reads isDisposed() between the setting of slot 0 and the other slots, it will correctly return true. However, if the array has 0 slots (capacity=0), get(0) will throw IndexOutOfBoundsException. Also, setResource() and replaceResource() individually check for CANCELLED per-slot, but isDisposed() only looks at slot 0, so slots with non-CANCELLED values could exist while isDisposed() reports true if slot 0 was set differently.
suspicions.suspected_bug: isDisposed() can throw IndexOutOfBoundsException if ArrayCompositeSubscription was constructed with capacity 0, or return inconsistent results if only some slots are set to CANCELLED.

suspicions.observation: SchedulerToExecutorService.shutdown() does: if (workerStore.get() instanceof Worker w) { w.dispose(); } else { var w = workerStore.getAndSet(SHUTDOWN); if (w != null) w.dispose(); }. The first branch reads the worker and disposes it but doesn't atomically replace it with SHUTDOWN. Another thread could set a new worker between get() and dispose(), causing a newly-set worker to be missed. Meanwhile, the else branch correctly uses getAndSet.
suspicions.suspected_bug: Race condition in shutdown(): the first branch (when workerStore contains a valid Worker) doesn't use getAndSet, so a concurrently updated worker may not be disposed, leading to resource leaks or inconsistent shutdown state.

suspicions.observation: ExecutorScheduler.Worker.dispose() does `if (getAndSet(null) != null)` to check for disposal, but `isDisposed()` checks `get() == null`. After `dispose()` sets the value to null, `isDisposed()` returns true. However, `schedule()` methods in ExecutorScheduler.Worker check `if (disposed)` (a volatile boolean field, line 639) before `get() == null`. The `dispose()` method sets the AtomicReference to null but does NOT set `disposed = true`. So `isDisposed()` returns true but the disposed boolean stays false, leading to the schedule() methods potentially still attempting to schedule after disposal, since they check the volatile `disposed` field instead of `isDisposed()`.
suspicions.suspected_bug: ExecutorScheduler.Worker.dispose() sets the AtomicReference to null but does not set the `disposed` volatile flag to true. The schedule() methods check `disposed` field, so after dispose(), they may still attempt to schedule work because `disposed` remains false, even though `isDisposed()` correctly returns true.

suspicions.observation: In ScheduledRunnable.run(), the finally block first reads `o = get(PARENT_INDEX)` and checks `o != PARENT_DISPOSED && compareAndSet(PARENT_INDEX, o, DONE) && o != null`. If `o` is a DisposableContainer, it casts and calls `delete(this)`. However, if between the `get(PARENT_INDEX)` read and the `compareAndSet` call, another thread has already replaced PARENT_INDEX with DONE, then `compareAndSet` fails, and the deletion from the parent container is skipped. This could lead to the parent container never being notified of this task's completion, causing a resource leak.
suspicions.suspected_bug: ScheduledRunnable.run() has a race in the PARENT_INDEX cleanup where a concurrent dispose() may set PARENT_INDEX to PARENT_DISPOSED after the get() but before compareAndSet, causing the parent DisposableContainer to never have delete(this) called. The task would be leaked from the parent's tracking.

suspicions.observation: VolatileSizeArrayList.set(int, T) delegates to list.set() but does NOT call lazySet(list.size()) afterwards. The set() operation doesn't change the size, but if concurrent operations are happening, the volatile size counter could become stale relative to the backing ArrayList's actual state, particularly if remove+set race or set is called after a failed CAS in another thread. However, the more important issue is: `set` doesn't call lazySet, which means the volatile size won't reflect the state properly after a set.
suspicions.suspected_bug: VolatileSizeArrayList.set() doesn't update the volatile size field via lazySet(), potentially causing stale reads. While set() doesn't change size, the lazySet serves as a memory fence ensuring visibility of the updated element across threads. Without it, other threads may not see the set element even when checking size().

suspicions.observation: SpscArrayQueue.offer(E v1, E v2) is a FIXME stub that just calls offer(v1) && offer(v2). Unlike SpscLinkedArrayQueue which has a dedicated optimized two-element offer, this is just a fallback. The issue is that if offer(v1) succeeds but offer(v2) fails due to capacity, the caller (which expects atomic two-element add) will see false return but v1 is already in the queue. This is inconsistent with the contract of SpscLinkedArrayQueue.offer(T, T) which either adds both or neither.
suspicions.suspected_bug: SpscArrayQueue.offer(E, E) is non-atomic - if the first element succeeds but the second fails due to capacity, the caller sees inconsistent state (v1 added but v2 not). Code depending on the atomic two-element guarantee (e.g., in queue fusion) may produce incorrect results or miss elements.

suspicions.observation: CachedWorkerPool.evictExpiredWorkers() iterates over a ConcurrentLinkedQueue and breaks on line 138 when it finds a non-expired worker, with the comment 'Queue is ordered with the worker that will expire first in the beginning'. However, ConcurrentLinkedQueue is a FIFO queue that doesn't maintain any ordering by expiration time. Workers released later (with later expiration times) are appended to the TAIL. So a worker with a LATER expiration time could be BEFORE a worker with an EARLIER expiration time in the queue. The early break skips potentially expired workers that are after the first non-expired one, causing stale workers to never be evicted (memory leak).
suspicions.suspected_bug: CachedScheduler.CachedWorkerPool.evictExpiredWorkers uses ConcurrentLinkedQueue and assumes it's ordered by expiration time, but ConcurrentLinkedQueue is FIFO. The early break on the first non-expired worker skips expired workers that come after it, causing memory leaks from leaked ThreadWorker instances.

suspicions.observation: SchedulerToExecutorService.invokeAll() submits all tasks to the scheduler, then calls f.get() on each Future in order. But since the scheduler dispatches tasks back to this same ExecutorService (via execute()), and f.get() blocks the calling thread, if the underlying scheduler runs tasks on the current thread (like TrampolineScheduler or ImmediateThinScheduler), this will deadlock. Additionally, the synchronous sequential f.get() defeats the parallel execution model of invokeAll.
suspicions.suspected_bug: SchedulerToExecutorService.invokeAll() can deadlock when used with schedulers that run on the calling thread (TrampolineScheduler, ImmediateThinScheduler) because f.get() blocks the calling thread while the scheduler needs that same thread to execute tasks.

suspicions.observation: Scheduler.toExecutorService() (line 392) creates `new SchedulerToExecutorService(this, null)` passing null for workerStore. But in SchedulerToExecutorService, execute() calls `workerStore.get() instanceof Worker w`, shutdown() calls `workerStore.get() instanceof Worker w`, and isShutdown() calls `workerStore.get()` — all of which will throw NullPointerException when workerStore is null. The @NonNull annotation on the record parameter is violated.
suspicions.suspected_bug: Scheduler.toExecutorService() passes null as workerStore, but SchedulerToExecutorService.execute(), shutdown(), isShutdown(), and other methods all call workerStore.get() without null-checking, causing immediate NPE when any method is invoked on the returned ExecutorService.

suspicions.observation: FlowableSampleTimed.SampleTimedEmitLast.run() does `if (wip.incrementAndGet() == 2)` to guard entry. If the timer fires twice before the first invocation decrements wip, the second call increments wip to 3 (not 2) and skips the block entirely without emitting or decrementing. This means wip grows by 1 permanently. When onComplete() calls complete() later, wip.decrementAndGet() won't reach 0, and downstream.onComplete() will never be called. The stream hangs silently.
suspicions.suspected_bug: FlowableSampleTimed.SampleTimedEmitLast has a wip counter that can grow unbounded when the periodic timer fires faster than drain completion, preventing downstream.onComplete() from ever being called. The stream hangs silently when complete() decrements but doesn't reach 0.

suspicions.observation: SchedulerToExecutorService.invokeAny() calls f.exceptionNow() on a CompletableFuture. In Java, CompletableFuture.exceptionNow() is designed for internal JDK use and throws IllegalStateException when the future was completed normally (not exceptionally). Since all submitted tasks complete normally, this always throws IllegalStateException in the isDone() check path.
suspicions.suspected_bug: invokeAny() throws IllegalStateException instead of returning results because CompletableFuture.exceptionNow() is misused - it throws when the future completed normally rather than exceptionally.

This means wip grows by 1 permanently. When onComplete() calls complete() later, wip.decrementAndGet() won't reach 0, and downstream.onComplete() will never be called. The stream hangs silently.

bugs.observation: VolatileSizeArrayList.set(int, T) delegates to list.set() but does NOT call lazySet(list.size()) afterwards. The set() operation doesn't change the size, but if concurrent operations are happening, the volatile size counter could become stale relative to the backing ArrayList's actual state, particularly if remove+set race or set is called after a failed CAS in another thread. However, the more important issue is: `set` doesn't call lazySet, which means the volatile size won't reflect the state properly after a set.
bugs.suspected_bug: VolatileSizeArrayList.set() doesn't update the volatile size field via lazySet(), potentially causing stale reads. While set() doesn't change size, the lazySet serves as a memory fence ensuring visibility of the updated element across threads. Without it, other threads may not see the set element even when checking size().
bugs.evidence: VolatileSizeArrayList.java:130 - set() calls only list.set() without lazySet(list.size()), unlike all other mutating methods, causing confirmed memory visibility failures
bugs.reproduction: Test fails on /src/new: "AssertionError: set() should establish happens-before via volatile write so element updates are visible". Same failure on /src/old. The reader thread sees stale value 0 instead of 42 because set() lacks lazySet(), providing no happens-before edge.

bugs.observation: SpscArrayQueue.offer(E v1, E v2) is a FIXME stub that just calls offer(v1) && offer(v2). Unlike SpscLinkedArrayQueue which has a dedicated optimized two-element offer, this is just a fallback. The issue is that if offer(v1) succeeds but offer(v2) fails due to capacity, the caller (which expects atomic two-element add) will see false return but v1 is already in the queue. This is inconsistent with the contract of SpscLinkedArrayQueue.offer(T, T) which either adds both or neither.
bugs.suspected_bug: SpscArrayQueue.offer(E, E) is non-atomic - if the first element succeeds but the second fails due to capacity, the caller sees inconsistent state (v1 added but v2 not). Code depending on the atomic two-element guarantee (e.g., in queue fusion) may produce incorrect results or miss elements.
